title: Resilience mechanisms in Parkinson’s disease: a domain-specific conceptual framework
title_zh: 帕金森病中的韧性机制：领域特定概念框架
abstract: Abstract While nigrostriatal dopaminergic cell loss is the pathological hallmark of Parkinson’s disease, it is well-known that dopamine deficiency cannot fully explain the clinical severity or disease progression. Emerging data suggest that resilience, i.e. the brain’s capacity to maintain function despite pathology, plays a key role in shaping clinical variability of both motor and non-motor symptoms. However, different contributing terms have been proposed, including brain compensation and reserve, and it remains unclear how these terms can be delineated both conceptually and mechanistically. Therefore, here we provide a synthesis of recent neuroimaging evidence on resilience mechanisms in Parkinson’s disease, with the following aims: (i) clarify the terminology; (ii) define the mechanisms; and (iii) relate resilience mechanisms to treatments, including dopamine replacement therapy and deep brain stimulation. We distinguish between compensation and reserve. We define compensation as adaptive neural activity that stabilizes task performance in the presence of pathology, particularly under increased demands, and is inversely related to clinical deficits. By contrast, reserve (cognitive or motor) refers to the capacity of neural resources that is built up across the lifetime, shaped by factors of an individual’s exposome. Compensation has been localized to the parieto-premotor network alongside the relatively preserved anterior striatum. Higher motor reserve has been linked to somatomotor network tolerance, preserved structural integrity and higher striatal functional network connectivity. Cognitive reserve relates to network robustness and structural integrity within the fronto-parietal network. Whether resilience mechanisms drive interindividual variability in long-term treatment response remains unresolved. Lower motor reserve predicts accelerated levodopa dose escalation and increased risk of dyskinesias, while cognitive reserve modulates both cognitive and motor outcomes after deep brain stimulation, highlighting cross-domain interactions. Brain compensation and reserve are two key components of resilience that together shape clinical heterogeneity in Parkinson’s disease across motor and cognitive domains. Although they operate at different timescales and through distinct mechanisms, they remain intrinsically related. Our framework suggests that biomarkers of resilience could complement biological definitions of Parkinson’s disease and shift therapeutic strategies from merely slowing degeneration towards strengthening adaptive capacity. Key priorities for future work are to define the longitudinal relationship between resilience failure and subcortical neurodegeneration using concurrent measures of nigrostriatal decline, multimodal datasets or controlled interventions, and to determine how symptom domain-specific resilience mechanisms shape treatment outcomes to enable targeted modulation and better capture disease heterogeneity.
abstract_zh: 摘要 虽然帕金森病中黑质纹状神经元的退化是其病理特征，但众所周知，多巴胺缺乏无法完全解释临床严重程度或疾病进展。新兴数据表明，韧性即大脑在病理情况下维持功能的能力，在塑造运动和非运动症状的临床变异性方面起关键作用。然而，已提出了不同的贡献术语，包括大脑补偿和储备，且尚不清楚如何在概念和机制上界定这些术语。因此，此处我们综合了帕金森病中关于韧性机制的最新神经影像学证据，旨在：（i）阐明术语；（ii）定义机制；（iii）将韧性机制与治疗相关联，包括多巴胺替代疗法和深脑刺激。我们区分了补偿与储备。我们将补偿定义为在病理情况下稳定任务表现的自适应神经活动，特别是在需求增加时，且与临床缺陷呈逆相关。相比之下，储备（认知或运动）是指一生中积累的神经资源容量，由个体 exposome 的因素塑造。补偿已定位到顶叶-运动网络以及相对保存的前纹状体。较高的运动储备与运动网络的耐受性、结构完整性得以保存以及更高的纹状体功能网络连接性相关。认知储备与前额叶-顶叶网络内的网络鲁棒性和结构完整性相关。韧性机制是否驱动长期治疗响应的个体间变异仍未解决。较低的运动储备预测左旋多巴剂量加快递增以及舞蹈症风险增加，而认知储备则在深脑刺激后调节认知和运动结果，突显了跨域相互作用。大脑补偿和储备是韧性的两个关键组成部分，它们共同塑造了帕金森病在运动和认知领域的临床异质性。虽然它们在不同时间尺度和通过不同机制运作，但它们仍然内在相关。我们的框架表明，韧性生物标志物可以补充帕金森病的生物学定义，并将治疗策略从单纯减缓退行转向增强适应能力。未来工作的关键优先事项是利用 nigrostriatal 下降的并发测量、多模态数据或受控干预来定义韧性失效与亚核退行的纵向关系，并确定特定症状领域的韧性机制如何塑造治疗结果，以实现靶向调节并更好地捕捉疾病异质性。
